question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{20}$ are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{n}∼N(n\mu ,\,n{\sigma }^{2}).
$$

Therefore, since ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{20}$ are independent and identically distributed, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{20} & ∼N(20\cdot 1,\,20\cdot {2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(20\cdot 1,\,20\cdot 4) \\  & =N(20,80).\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to compute the probability $P(Y\le 21).$ We first convert $Y$ into a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 21) & =P(Z\le \frac{21-20}{\sqrt{80}}) \\  & =P(Z\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{80}}) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.11) \\  & =Φ(0.11)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we have

$$
Φ(0.11)=0.5438.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(Y\le 21)=Φ(0.11)=0.5438.
$$
